title: Getting Started — Topology B: Direct Ethernet Cable (PC to PS2)
text: Topology B: Direct Ethernet Cable (PC to PS2). Connect an Ethernet cable directly between the PC's network jack and the PS2. Modern PC network interfaces support Auto-MDIX (automatic crossover), so a standard patch cable works fine. Assign your PC's Ethernet adapter a manual static IP: 192.168.0.1 (Subnet: 255.255.255.0 ). Assign the PS2 a static IP in the same subnet: 192.168.0.2 . Leave Gateway blank or set to 192.168.0.1 .

title: Getting Started — 2. Prepare Your Library or Block Image
text: 2. Prepare Your Library or Block Image. For UDPFS, SMB, and HTTP: create a dedicated game-library folder (for example D:\PS2Games on Windows or /srv/ps2 on Linux) and organize it with the standard OPL hierarchy: PS2Games/ ├── CD/ ← CD-based PS2 games (<700 MB ISO images) ├── DVD/ ← DVD5 and DVD9 PS2 games (>700 MB ISO images) ├── ART/ ← Cover art, backgrounds, spines, discs (optional) ├── CFG/ ← Per-game configuration files (optional) ├── VMC/ ← 8MB Virtual Memory Card files (optional) └── CHT/ ← Cheats files (optional) Folder Case Sensitivity & Disc Naming Ensure folder names are in UPPERCASE ( DVD , CD , ART ). Many loaders (and Linux/Edge servers) are case-sensitive. For best compatibility, name your games using the standard OPL startup identifier convention: DVD/SLUS_201.74.Rumble Racing.iso or CD/SCUS_971.24.Game.iso . For UDPBD: do not select this library directory. Select one image file in the UDPBD card instead. Its internal format must match what the console-side block driver expects. Enable Read-only for your first test. See the UDPBD setup steps .

title: Getting Started — Download and Extract
text: Download and Extract. Download the latest release package from the Releases Page . Extract the portable ZIP to a folder on your host machine. Launch PS2Servers.exe on Windows, or invoke python ps2servers.py from source.

title: Getting Started — Choose Your LAN Interface
text: Choose Your LAN Interface. In the top bar of PS2 Servers Desktop, ensure the LAN IP dropdown selects the network adapter wired to your PS2. The launcher automatically displays the IP address and helpful setup hints for each card.

title: Getting Started — Select the Right Path & Start
text: Select the Right Path & Start. On UDPFS / SMB / HTTP , browse to the parent folder containing DVD/ and CD/ . On UDPBD , browse to a single image file ; do not choose the game-library folder. Press Start , then check Terminal for the image/root path and a successful listening message. Firewall Notice When starting a server for the first time, Windows Defender Firewall may prompt to allow network traffic. Check Private networks and click Allow access . PS2 Servers also provides an automatic firewall rule creator in the application settings. External-drive access After selecting a folder or image file, click Check access on the server card. The results appear in a dialog and the Terminal log. Folder checks verify listing only; image checks verify reading and, unless read-only is selected, a writable open without writing data. Actual game reads and saves still need testing. On Linux, check parent-directory access and mount ownership/permissions; NTFS/exFAT mount options can control access. On Windows, check the target's Security permissions for your account. This check does not open raw disks, reformat drives, or change permissions.

text: 4. Configure Network in Your Loader. Boot your PlayStation 2, launch your loader, and navigate to Network Settings . There is no SMB share, username, or password. The PS2 still needs its own working IP configuration. The Desktop LAN IP selector provides hints; it does not bind all server sockets. title: Getting Started — 5. Launch Your First Game
text: 5. Launch Your First Game. These game-list steps apply to filesystem/game-library protocols such as UDPFS, SMB, and compatible HTTP clients. UDPBD exposes a block device and does not provide a DVD/ directory listing. Save your loader's network configuration to your Memory Card ( mc0: ). Return to the main menu and press the button to refresh the game list (in OPL/RiptOPL, scroll to the ETH / Netboot tab or press Select / Circle ). Your game list should populate with titles from your DVD/ and CD/ folders. Highlight your game, press X (Cross) or Start , and enjoy!

title: Getting Started — Common Questions & Troubleshooting
text: Common Questions & Troubleshooting. My loader says "cannot open folder" or displays "mass0:" while using UDPBD. mass0: may be a logical device/mount identifier used by that loader; the label alone does not prove it is a physical USB device. Verify the console-side backend genuinely supports UDPBD, the server is serving one image file rather than a folder, and the client understands that image's format. If you expected to browse a collection of ISO files, use UDPFS or SMB at both ends . Read the UDPBD diagnosis checklist . The server is running but there is no connection. Which IP and port? The PC and PS2 need different IP addresses on a reachable local network. SMB uses the actual displayed TCP port and share; HTTP requires its configured TCP port; UDPFS discovers via UDP 62966 plus an optional data port; UDPBD uses UDP 48573 broadcast discovery. Allow the corresponding traffic through the host firewall, and verify that broadcasts can cross your current switch/router configuration. The game list is empty after connecting. What should I check? title: Editions & Architecture — Which Edition Should You Choose?
text: Which Edition Should You Choose?. Choose Desktop if you are playing on Windows, macOS, or a Linux workstation and want a simple visual launcher with start/stop buttons and automatic configuration saving. Choose Core if you have an existing Linux server with Python installed, run games from Docker containers, or want to script headless background services. Choose Edge if you want to run servers 24/7 on an OpenWrt router, Raspberry Pi, home NAS, or old low-power hardware without a monitor or desktop environment. Choose Desktop/Core if you have disc images in CHD format , or require SMB2/SMB3 authenticated sharing or HTTP game streaming .

title: UDPFS Server
text: UDPFS Server UDPFS (User Datagram Protocol File System) is the modern, lightweight network streaming protocol built specifically for PlayStation 2 homebrew. It eliminates SMB overhead, supports on-the-fly decompression of disc images, and powers network booting in Neutrino , NHDDL , and RiptOPL . Why UDPFS? Unlike SMB, which requires TCP state machines, SMB dialect negotiation, session handshakes, and strict authentication trees, UDPFS operates over raw UDP datagrams. The protocol is connection-oriented at the application layer, dramatically reducing CPU and memory overhead on the PS2's Input/Output Processor (IOP). 1. Ports & Network Architecture By default, UDPFS operates in a two-port model : Socket Port Purpose Discovery Port UDP 62966 ( 0xF5F6 ) Listens for broadcast discovery probes and initial connection requests from the PS2 console. Data Port Dynamic (or Pinned e.g. 62967 ) Dedicated high-speed socket created for the session to handle file reads, directory listings, and block operations. Firewall Configuration for Two-Port Operation If you run a firewall with strict port rules, set an explicit Data port (such as 62967 ) on the UDPFS card or use CLI flag --data-port 62967 , and allow both UDP 62966 and 62967. Alternatively, CLI flag --single-port forces discovery and data over the single port 62966. 2. Resolving "Games List But Fail to Launch" The single most frequent support question is: "My games show up in the menu, but when I click launch, the screen goes black and nothing happens." This is almost always caused by a dual-interface routing issue on the host PC. When a computer has active Wi-Fi and wired Ethernet simultaneously, the operating system's routing table may send UDP data replies out of the Wi-Fi adapter instead of the Ethernet cable connected to the PS2. Identify Your PS2-Facing Network Interface Look at the LAN IP selector at the top of the PS2 Servers window and ensure you select the adapter physically cabled to your PS2 (for example 192.168.1.100 ). Pin the UDPFS Bind Address On the UDPFS server card, locate Bind address (PC) and click the button Use LAN IP (or type that IP directly). Do NOT type 0.0.0.0 or the PS2's IP here; enter the PC's own interface IP. Restart the Server Click Stop on the UDPFS card, then click Start . Relaunch your game from the console menu. title: UDPFS Server — 3. Protocol Modes: Auto, Standard, and Modulo
text: 3. Protocol Modes: Auto, Standard, and Modulo. Over the years, different homebrew loaders introduced divergent implementations of the UDPFS protocol: Standard Mode (upstream udpfsd): Uses 4KB data blocks, separate discovery and data sockets, and sequence-based acknowledgment. Used by modern Neutrino and RiptOPL. Modulo Mode (legacy NHDDL): Employs a single socket with modulo-sequence packet pacing and smaller block buffers. Auto Mode (Default in PS2 Servers): PS2 Servers dynamically inspects the initial connection probe from the client and automatically adapts its sequencing and protocol mode on a per-session basis. Leave Protocol Mode on Auto Keep Protocol mode: Auto selected. Do not check Enforce Modulo mode unless you are explicitly testing an older NHDDL build that fails during the initial handshake. Forcing Modulo mode is never the solution for a network interface binding issue.

text: SMB Server (v1 / v2 / v3) Server Message Block (SMB) remains the standard network sharing protocol for Open PS2 Loader (OPL) and RiptOPL . PS2 Servers provides user-space SMBv1, SMB2, and SMB3 server engines that eliminate the need to enable obsolete or insecure Windows OS features. Dialect Rule: Choose What Your Loader Supports An SMBv1-only loader cannot connect to an SMB2/3 server simply because both cards point to the same games folder. title: UDPBD Server — Exclusive raw access and writes
text: Exclusive raw access and writes. Enable Exclusive raw access ( --exclusive ) to unmount Linux filesystems and exclusively claim the device, or lock then dismount affected Windows volumes. Locks remain held until shutdown. Busy, boot/system and unknown targets abort startup. Windows never force-dismounts a volume when locking fails. Linux filesystems remain unmounted afterward; remount them explicitly. Startup failure may leave some Linux mounts unmounted. Check access never locks, dismounts or tests writes. For VMC saves, explicitly enable Enable raw writes / VMC ( --raw-write ) with Exclusive access enabled and Read-only disabled. Use only a dedicated non-system game drive on a trusted LAN: UDPBD has no authentication, and a client can write every exposed sector. Writes are bounded, native-sector aligned and flushed before acknowledgement, but an interrupted/failed write can be partial. Real-drive and PS2 VMC behavior remain experimental. python ps2servers.py serve udpbd --raw-device /dev/disk/by-id/YOUR-DRIVE --exclusive --raw-write

title: UDPBD Server — Virtual exFAT folder

This exposes ordinary files through an MBR disk with one exFAT partition; no disk formatting, full image copy, raw-device privileges or unmounting is required. The client must support exFAT. Contents are read lazily with metadata frozen at startup. Keep the folder unchanged and restart to refresh it. Changed file identity, size or modification time causes a read error. text: 5. Troubleshooting: Cannot Open Folder, mass0:, or No Image. The loader says "cannot open folder" and displays mass0: . Do not assume mass0: means a physical USB drive. It may be a client-side logical device or mount name. The message alone neither proves that UDPBD discovery succeeded nor shows what filesystem the loader attempted. Check the active loader backend, the supplied image format, and whether the client is trying to enumerate folders from a raw block device. For a folder of ISOs, use UDPFS/SMB or Virtual exFAT with an exFAT-capable UDPBD client. Broadcast normally stays within a LAN; guest Wi-Fi, VLANs, VPNs and routed subnets can isolate devices. Check for a UDPBD_CMD_INFO from ... line while the client probes. title: HTTP Game Streaming
text: HTTP Game Streaming HTTP Mode serves your PS2 game collection over standard plain HTTP for compatible OPL forks (such as Docmine17's Open-PS2-Loader-HTTP and RiptOPL ). By replacing SMB with standard HTTP Range requests, it eliminates complex network authentication entirely. Experimental Status HTTP game serving is host-tested and functional across compliant clients. Because loader support across diverse hardware remains under active community development, report findings to the project issue tracker. 1. Setting Up HTTP Mode  Start the HTTP Server Card Select your games folder (the parent holding DVD/ and CD/ ) and start the HTTP card. The default port is TCP 1100 . Configure Your Console Loader In OPL Network Settings, configure the following values: Field Required Value Protocol HTTP Address Type IP PC IP Address IP address shown on the running HTTP card Port 1100 (Must be set explicitly) Share Name Blank, or anything (ignored by server) Critical Client Quirk: Set Port Explicitly In the pinned Docmine17 HTTP client, leaving Port set to 0 causes its game-list loader to default to port 8080 while its in-game driver defaults to port 1100 ! The result is that your game list populates, but selecting a game produces an immediate black screen. Always set Port to 1100 explicitly in your loader. 2. What the Server Serves The HTTP server inspects your games folder root, DVD/ , and CD/ , automatically generating two resources: games.csv — Generated on the fly at /games.csv and /<share>/games.csv . Lists startup identifiers, titles, and media types without manual curation. Bare Game ISOs: Disc images are flattened at the web root (e.g. GET /SLUS_201.74.Rumble Racing.iso ) to accommodate the console driver's hardcoded root path. 3. Compressed Format Streaming Format Handling Mechanism .iso Streamed directly via HTTP Range headers. .zso , .ziso Streamed compressed as-is. The PS2 client decompresses LZ4 blocks locally. .chd , .cso Decompressed in real time on the server and advertised to the client as standard .iso . 4. Known Limits & Specifications Read-Only Protocol: The HTTP client driver does not support WebDAV or HTTP PUT; Virtual Memory Cards (VMC) cannot be written over HTTP. Saves require a physical memory card. No Authentication: Never expose port 1100 to the public internet; keep it strictly on your local private subnet. Single-Layer Discs Only: The client driver hardcodes layer1_start = 0 , so dual-layer DVD9 titles will not transition beyond the layer break

title: PS2 Servers Edge
text: PS2 Servers Edge PS2 Servers Edge is a high-speed, statically linked Go implementation engineered for routers, network-attached storage (NAS), Raspberry Pi, and minimal Linux appliances. It operates with a sub-20 MB RAM footprint and provides a responsive, embedded Web GUI dashboard. Why Edge Exists Running a full Python interpreter and desktop UI on an embedded MIPS/ARM router or an old thin client is often impossible due to flash storage and RAM constraints. Edge eliminates all Python dependencies, compiling down to a single compact binary that starts instantaneously and runs 24/7 beside your console. 1. Protocol & Feature Scope Edge implements the most critical network-serving protocols for PS2 homebrew: Implemented in Edge UDPFS Engine: Full read and write support; automatic per-session Standard/Modulo negotiation; multi-console concurrency. UDPBD Block Device: Direct sector serving for raw disc images over UDP 48573. SMBv1 Server: Guest-authenticated file sharing on TCP 1111 for standard OPL. Embedded Web UI: Responsive web management console for LAN monitoring and service control. CSO & ZSO Decoding: Decompresses CSO and ZSO disc containers on the fly with a bounded block cache. title: OpenWrt Router Setup

By running PS2 Servers Edge directly on OpenWrt with a USB storage drive, you can play your entire library over Ethernet with zero PC running. Why an OpenWrt Router Server? Home routers are always powered on, consume less than 5 Watts of electricity, and feature direct gigabit/fast Ethernet switching to your entertainment center. Edge requires under 20 MB of RAM, leaving plenty of headroom for normal routing and Wi-Fi duties. 1. Prerequisites A home router running modern OpenWrt (version 21.02, 22.03, 23.05, or newer). A USB 2.0 or USB 3.0 port on the router. An external USB flash drive, external SSD, or HDD formatted in ext4 , exFAT , or FAT32 . Mounting USB Storage on OpenWrt Log in to your router via SSH and install the necessary filesystem kernel modules: # Update package list and install storage drivers opkg update opkg install kmod-usb-storage block-mount kmod-fs-ext4 kmod-fs-exfat kmod-fs-vfat e2fsprogs # Identify your connected USB drive partition block info Create a mount point (e.g. /mnt/ps2games ) and enable auto-mounting via /etc/config/fstab or the LuCI web interface under System → Mount Points . 3. title: Router & Server Status
text: Router & Server Status PS2 Servers includes a lightweight, broadcast-based status discovery protocol. This allows desktop management tools, monitoring scripts, and client launchers to detect running server instances and query real-time operational telemetry across the local network. Discovery Protocol Summary By broadcasting a small probe packet to UDP port 62966 , any device on the LAN can identify active Edge routers, active server services (SMB, UDPFS, UDPBD), and current streaming throughput without needing SSH credentials. 1. Protocol Specification The status discovery protocol operates over raw UDP datagrams: Field Specification Port UDP 62966 (or configured status port) Probe Format Short magic broadcast query Reply Format JSON / structured telemetry payload containing hostname, version, running subcommands, and active client counts 2. Querying Status from the Terminal You can query any PS2 Servers instance using a simple Python snippet or netcat: python -c " import socket s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_BROADCAST, 1) s.settimeout(2.0) s.sendto(b'PS2S_STATUS_PROBE', ('255.255.255.255', 62966)) try: data, addr = s.recvfrom(2048) print(f'Server reply from {addr}: {data.decode()}') except socket.timeout: print('No server response on LAN') " 3. Edge Status Configuration In Edge, status replies are enabled by default on the discovery port. If multiple processes share a machine, or if you wish to disable telemetry replies, use the following options: --status-port -1 — Default: uses primary UDPFS port 62966. --status-port 0 — Completely disables status discovery replies on this process. --status-port PORT — Binds status replies to a dedicated custom UDP port.

title: Compressed Disc Formats
text: Compressed Disc Formats PS2 Servers supports compressed disc formats, enabling you to store large game libraries in a fraction of the disk space while streaming them seamlessly to your PlayStation 2. Server-Side vs Client-Side Decompression There are two ways compressed images are streamed: Client-Side Decoding (ZSO): The server transfers compressed LZ4 blocks directly over the network; the PS2's processor decompresses them in RAM. This minimizes network traffic. Server-Side Decoding (CHD & CSO): The host PC or router decompresses requested sectors in real time and delivers raw optical disc sectors to the console. The console never knows the file is compressed. 1. Format Comparison Matrix Format Algorithm Typical Storage Reduction Console Decoding Server Decoding Support Raw ISO ( .iso ) None (Uncompressed) 0% Native Desktop · Core · Edge ZSO ( .zso , .ziso ) LZ4 (2048-byte blocks) 20% – 45% Native in OPL / RiptOPL Desktop · Core · Edge CSO ( .cso , .ciso ) Deflate / zlib 25% – 50% Limited / High IOP load Desktop · Core · Edge CHD ( .chd ) LZMA / FLAC / zlib 35% – 65% (Best) None Desktop · Core (via libchdr ) 2. Optional Compression Dependencies PS2 Servers Desktop and Core automatically inspect the Python environment for optional acceleration and decompression modules: libchdr — Required for CHD format decompression. Included in pre-compiled Desktop packages; installable via pip install libchdr in source mode. lz4 — Accelerates ZSO block parsing and verification. zstandard — Provides Zstandard dictionary acceleration. Desktop Dependency Panel In PS2 Servers Desktop, click Settings → Dependencies to inspect the detected status of all optional compression libraries. If a library is missing, Desktop displays exact installation commands for your OS. 3. Compressing Your Disc Images  Compressing to ZSO (Recommended for Console Compatibility) Use maxcso to compress raw DVD ISOs into high-speed ZSO images: maxcso --format=zso --block=2048 game.iso -o DVD/SLUS_201.74.Game.zso Compressing to CHD (Best Compression Ratio) Use chdman (from the MAME toolset) to achieve maximum compression for Desktop/Core serving: # For DVD games: chdman createdvd -i game.iso -o DVD/SLUS_201.74.Game.chd # For CD games (from CUE/BIN): chdman createcd -i game.cue -o CD/SLUS_201.74.Game.chd

title: Protocol Compatibility
text: Protocol Compatibility & Wire Specs In-depth technical breakdown of protocol implementations across Desktop/Core (Python) and Edge (Go), packet-level wire specifications, and homebrew client support matrix. Specification Parity PS2 Servers maintains 100% wire-protocol parity with canonical specifications: the udpfsd specification by pcm720, the UDPBD block driver specification, and the Microsoft SMBv1 / SMB2 / SMB3 network contracts. 1. Console Homebrew Compatibility Matrix Loader support varies by project and version. Review this matrix to match your loader to the correct server mode: Loader / Application SMBv1 SMB2 / SMB3 UDPFS UDPBD HTTP RiptOPL Full Support Full Support Full Support Full Support Full Support Official OPL (ps2homebrew) Full Support Not in stock Not in stock Not in stock Not in stock Neutrino (Core) via SMB module No Native Primary Native Primary No NHDDL (Neutrino GUI) No No Native Primary Native Primary No Open-PS2-Loader-HTTP (Docmine17) No No No No Native Primary 2. Core (Python) vs Edge (Go) Wire Differences While both implementations produce compatible network flows, they differ in several low-level operational details: Socket Binding Semantics Core (Python): Passing --bind IP binds only the dynamically allocated data socket; the discovery listener continues to listen on 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces) to catch broadcasts. Edge (Go): Passing --bind IP binds both the discovery socket and the data socket to that explicit IP. CSO/ZSO Cache Architectures Core (Python): Relies on OS page cache and Python's memory view slices for sector buffering. Edge (Go): Implements an explicit, fixed-size ring cache for decompressed sector blocks, maintaining predictable sub-20MB memory ceilings on embedded routers. 3. UDPFS Packet Structure UDPFS packets start with a fixed 16-byte header: +----------------+----------------+----------------+----------------+ | Magic (0xF5F6) | Command (16b) | Sequence (32b) | Length (32b) | +----------------+----------------+----------------+----------------+ | File Handle / Session ID (32b) | Payload Data (0 - 4096 bytes) | +---------------------------------+---------------------------------+ Commands include OPEN , READ , WRITE , CLOSE , READDIR , and STAT . Standard mode limits payload frames to 4096 bytes, aligning cleanly with the PS2 IOP's network buffer allocations.

title: UDPFS Diagnostics
text: UDPFS Handoff & Diagnostics Step-by-step diagnostic methodologies for troubleshooting UDPFS connection issues, interpreting server log prefixes, and utilizing the 45-second inactivity telemetry report. Observability First A server log that simply goes quiet cannot tell you what failed on its own. PS2 Servers Core includes active network-probing diagnostics that distinguish between console IOP crashes, driver read errors, and packet routing stalls. 1. Decoding Server Log Prefixes Every incoming packet logged in PS2 Servers Core begins with a client endpoint prefix: [192.168.1.150:62966] Discovery probe received (seq=0) [192.168.1.150:62966] Session created -> data socket assigned 62967 [192.168.1.150:62967] OPEN DVD/SLUS_201.74.Rumble Racing.iso (flags=1) Client IP Changes During Launch If you see the IP change midway through booting (e.g. from 192.168.1.150 during game browsing to 192.168.0.10 on launch), the launched loader or game-specific configuration has a different static IP configured in its network driver. Ensure static IPs match across all configuration screens. Repeated Discovery (seq=0 Loops) If the server logs repeated seq=0 probes without advancing to data reads, the console is broadcasting discovery packets but cannot receive the server's reply. Check that the server's reply is not routed out of a secondary network interface (Wi-Fi). 2. The 45-Second Inactivity Diagnostic When a console with active open files stops communicating for 45 seconds, PS2 Servers Core sends an active ARP probe and evaluates the network interface, printing one of three definitive diagnostic verdicts: Verdict 1: "Still sending" Meaning: The console is continuing to transmit UDP packets, but they are out of sequence or corrupted. Cause: Packet loss or high latency on the network path. Ensure the connection is wired and that no conflicting UDP traffic saturates the link. Verdict 2: "Still answers ARP" Meaning: The PS2's network adapter is fully alive and responding to low-level link layer probes, but the game loader driver has ceased requesting data. Cause: Neutrino and OPL drivers halt completely after a single unrecoverable disc read error. The log lines immediately preceding this message identify the exact sector or file that caused the failure (e.g. bad disc dump, unsupported compression container). title: Antivirus Transparency & Trust
text: Antivirus Transparency & Trust PS2 Servers is a 100% open-source, community-driven network utility. Because it binds to local network sockets, handles raw datagrams, and is packaged without commercial code-signing certificates, heuristic antivirus engines may flag downloaded binaries as false positives. Core Trust Statement A generic detection label (such as Win32/Wacatac or Generic.Malware ) does not prove that a binary contains malicious code; it indicates that an automated heuristic rule matched patterns common to binary packers. Every line of source code in PS2 Servers is publicly auditable on GitHub. 1. Why Heuristics Flag PS2 Servers  Self-Extracting Packaging (Nuitka / PyInstaller) Single-file desktop executables bundle the Python interpreter, runtime DLLs, and server scripts into a compressed archive. When run, the stub extracts these files into a temporary directory ( %TEMP% ) and launches an unprivileged child process. Heuristic engines often flag any unpacker stub that extracts and executes code. Network Socket Binding PS2 Servers listens on low-level TCP and UDP ports (such as SMB port 1025/1111 and UDPFS port 62966). Software that opens network listener sockets without a commercially purchased digital signature is routinely treated with suspicion by heuristic algorithms. Lack of Commercial Code Signing Microsoft and commercial antivirus vendors give high trust ratings to executables signed with Extended Validation (EV) certificates. EV certificates cost hundreds of dollars annually and require corporate registration, which is prohibitive for free open-source hobbyist software. 2. Portable Builds: The Recommended Choice To reduce false positives, we provide portable archives ( PS2Servers-windows-x64-portable.zip ). The portable package contains all libraries and executables pre-extracted in a standard folder. Because portable builds do not use runtime self-extraction wrappers, they trigger significantly fewer heuristic alarms and launch noticeably faster. 3. How to Verify Downloaded Files Never bypass security warnings blindly. You can verify that your download has not been tampered with through cryptographic proofs: Compare SHA-256 Checksums: Verify that the hash of your file matches the official SHA256SUMS.txt attached to the GitHub release. title: Planned Features: NBD & ps2client
text: Planned Features: NBD & ps2client Architectural vision for extending PS2 Servers with Network Block Device (NBD) capabilities and ps2client developer instrumentation. Roadmap Feature This specification defines planned integrations currently undergoing prototyping and architectural evaluation. 1. The Two Directions of NBD The standard Linux Network Block Device (NBD) protocol enables block devices to be served over TCP port 10809 . Within the PS2 ecosystem, this serves two transformative workflows: Direction 1: PS2 HDD Export to PC (Internal HDD Management) The PS2 console boots a dedicated NBD server ELF, exposing its internal APA / exFAT 3.5" or 2.5" hard drive over Ethernet. A PC mounts the PS2's internal drive as a native block device using WinNBD (Windows) or nbd-client (Linux). Key Benefit: Allows users to copy ISOs, manage partitions, and backup saves at full 100Mbps Ethernet speeds without ever having to physically unscrew the network adapter or risk damaging 24-year-old IDE/SATA connector pins. Direction 2: PC Block Image Export to PS2 PS2 Servers serves raw disc images and virtual drives over standard NBD (TCP 10809) as an alternative to UDPBD. Loaders with an NBD client driver mount remote PC storage directly with TCP flow control. 2. ps2client Integration ps2client is the standard CLI utility for communicating with ps2link over Ethernet for homebrew developers. Integrating ps2client into the PS2 Servers Desktop launcher will allow: One-click remote execution of ELFs directly on the console over LAN. Live in-app streaming of PS2 kernel `printf` debugging logs (TTY output). Remote console reboot and power management.
